sut_family: scipy.fft.fht (fast Hankel transform) -- the rfft -> multiply-by-coefficients -> irfft real-FFT pipeline underlying scipy.fft's real-transform / Hermitian-symmetry surface
cat: G symmetry (Hermitian-symmetry preservation of the real-FFT (rfft/irfft) round-trip)
bug_introduced_commit: 36ae01b16d (ENH: fast Hankel transform #13084, born in v1.7.0)
pre_version_range_fired: v1.7.0 through v1.14.1 inclusive (buggy line present in all)
tolerance: 7.28e16 (scipy's own maintainer-chosen pass threshold for regression test test_gh_21661; the signature is far-tail-underflow-dominated, see honesty_caveat)
mr_used: f(r)=r^(mu+1)*exp(-r^2/2) is a SELF-DUAL Hankel pair: its order-mu Hankel transform equals f evaluated on the conjugate grid k=exp(offset)/flip(r). A correct fast Hankel transform (implemented as out=irfft(rfft(a)*u, n)) must reproduce f(k) for ANY transform length n; this holds iff the coefficient array u respects the rfft Hermitian-conjugate layout. The last rfft bin (index n//2) is the self-conjugate Nyquist bin -- hence real -- ONLY when n is EVEN; for ODD n that index is an ordinary non-self-conjugate coefficient whose imaginary part carries information. EVEN n is a control (output bit-identical pre/post); ODD n is the trigger.
fired_type: NUMERIC (silent wrong transform for odd length). fhtcoeff() unconditionally executed `u.imag[-1] = 0`, zeroing the imaginary part of a NON-Nyquist rfft coefficient for odd n and breaking Hermitian-symmetry consistency. PRE odd n=129: max rel-err vs analytic f(k) = 7.288256e+16 (>= scipy threshold 7.28e16 -> regression test FAILS). NOT a crash. EVEN n=128 control: 1.140775e+11, bit-identical pre/post.
verified: PIP RELEASED-TO-RELEASED self-run (uv venv py3.11, numpy 2.0.2): PRE scipy==1.14.1 FIRED -- fhtcoeff has unconditional `u.imag[-1]=0`; odd n=129 rel-err 7.288256e+16 >= 7.28e16. POST scipy==1.15.0 HELD -- fhtcoeff guards with `if n % 2 == 0: u.imag[-1]=0`; odd n=129 rel-err 7.225484e+16 < 7.28e16. Even n=128 identical (1.140775e+11) in both, confirming the fix touches only odd-length transforms.
array_api_gated: NO. fhtcoeff is pure numpy (np.linspace / np.empty(dtype=complex) / np.exp / scipy.special.loggamma / the literal numpy `u.imag[-1]` assignment); in fht/ifht it is computed first and only afterwards converted via xp.asarray(...). No is_array_api_strict / array_namespace dispatch guards the buggy line. The bug shipped in v1.7.0 (2021), ~5 releases BEFORE scipy.fft gained array-API support (v1.12.0), so it is the opposite of an array-API dev-regression -- it satisfies the 'non-SCIPY_ARRAY_API, plain-numpy backend' requirement.
honesty_caveat: The observable signature is EDGE-DOMINATED and numerically MARGINAL, not a clean order-of-magnitude blow-up. The maximum relative error sits at a single far-tail conjugate-grid point where f(k) underflows, so the pre/post separation occurs at an enormous magnitude (~7.2e16) and the scipy maintainers used a deliberately loose pass threshold (7.28e16); the repro uses that exact threshold as the FIRED/HELD boundary. On smooth, well-conditioned inputs (e.g. pure power laws r^gamma, scipy's test_fht_exact n in {64,63}) the corrupted top coefficient carries negligible energy and BOTH parities pass pre-fix (rel-err ~1e-14), i.e. the bug does NOT fire there. This is the cleanest non-array-API released-to-released scipy.fft Hermitian-symmetry bug found, but the previously-recorded 'scipy G scarce' caveat remains substantively true: scipy has no clean numpy-backend rfft/irfft/hfft symmetry bug that fires with a large margin on natural inputs; this one fires only via scipy's own contrived self-dual construction at a single underflow edge point.
